lines.text: Meet ChargeOne, the road trip co-pilot for electric cars in India.
The first screen says what you get, in plain words. You don't need to sign in to start.
Pick your car. It comes to life in your paint colour, with its battery size and an estimated highway range.
Now that it knows your car, ChargeOne offers a full week of Plus, free. Or stay on Basic, which anyone can use without signing in.
One map shows chargers from many companies, and drivers report whether they're working.
Once you're signed in, one tap starts the free Plus week. The ring counts down the days left.
In the Car tab, connect your car. This is the demo car, clearly labelled, on a simulated drive along the Mumbai Pune expressway.
Speed, power, energy per kilometre, battery temperature, and a battery health estimate, all update live.
Mahindra, Tata and MG don't offer other apps a public way to read their connected car data yet. So ChargeOne uses your phone's GPS, or a Bluetooth OBD adapter, in beta.
Plus members get a trip co-pilot. Ask it anything about charging, routes, or your car.
And you can plan the whole trip by voice, in Hindi or English.
कोयंबटूर से चेन्नई जाना है, बैटरी साठ प्रतिशत है।
कोयंबटूर से चेन्नई का प्लान बना रहा हूँ, बैटरी साठ प्रतिशत।
ChargeOne compares up to three routes, and explains each one: the fastest, the one with more fast chargers, and any that aren't safe on your battery.
Start the drive. Your battery forecast for every stop updates live, as you go.
If the battery drains faster than planned, ChargeOne warns you early, and offers a charger before the one you planned.
One tap switches to it, and the plan updates.
After each trip, drivers can rate their experience, and send ideas straight to us.
Basic is free for everyone. Plus adds the co-pilot, live drive alerts, and car connection, with seven days free. Coming first to Google Play, then the App Store.
